task.description: RE-CHECK (WF-03 Step 4) of ELIXIR-DEV's implementation (step-03b) of the corrected design (step-04c PASS): confirm the 6 Admission-gated sweeps now derive max_concurrency live from Letflow.Admission.global_cap/0 instead of the hardcoded literal 8 this same gate FAILED at step-04, independently re-run the previously-failing tests and the mutation test, run the full suite to completion, and give a final idiom/scope verdict on the whole diff before authorizing TEST-DESIGNER.

result.summary:
Independently re-verified every claim in step-03b/step-04c rather than accepting them on report. All checks pass; gap is genuinely closed.

1. FIX CONFIRMED IN THE REAL DIFF (not the handoff's paraphrase): ran `git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0421-20260904 -- lib/letflow/admission.ex lib/letflow/scheduler.ex lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` myself and read it in full. `Letflow.Admission.global_cap/1` is added as a byte-for-byte mirror of the already-approved `reserved_headroom/1` (GenServer.call delegate to a new `handle_call(:global_cap, _from, state)` clause replying `state.global_cap` unchanged -- no state-shape change, `global_cap` was already a state field). All 6 gated call sites in poller.ex (`poll_and_fire`, `retention_sweep`, `alert_detection`, `ordering_cycle`, `ordering_sweeper`, `ordering_metrics`) now read `run_sweep(schemas, :OP, Admission.global_cap(), fn ...)` -- the literal `8` module attribute is gone entirely (grep confirms zero remaining occurrences of the old `@admission_gated_max_concurrency` bound). `Admission.global_cap()` is evaluated as a plain function-call argument at each `run_sweep/4` call site, i.e. fresh on every tick and every sweep invocation -- never hoisted to a module attribute or cached local, exactly matching the corrected design and mirroring the pre-existing `maybe_refresh_active_instances/1` / `Admission.reserved_headroom()` convention.

2. TEST FILE GENUINELY UNTOUCHED: `git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0421-20260904 -- test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` is empty (0 lines) -- confirmed by direct diff, not taken on ELIXIR-DEV's word.

3. INDEPENDENT TEST RE-RUN: `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` run by me, in the foreground, to completion (43.0s): `31 passed`, 0 failed. Matches ELIXIR-DEV's reported 31/31 exactly, reproduced independently rather than trusted.

4. INDEPENDENT MUTATION-TEST RE-CONFIRMATION: sed-substituted all 6 `Admission.global_cap()` call sites in poller.ex back to the literal `8` myself, re-ran `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: `12/16 passed, 4 failed` -- the same 4 REQ-218 tests (AC1, AC2, AC3 per-schema clause, AC5) failed again under the reintroduced literal, confirming the test suite genuinely catches a regression back to a hardcoded bound at this repo's `pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 2 -> global_cap: 1` test config. Reverted immediately after (restored `Admission.global_cap()` at all 6 sites via the backed-up original file, confirmed via `git diff --stat` showing zero diff and a clean `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`).

5. FULL SUITE RUN TO COMPLETION (blocked in the foreground across multiple chained waits, ~28 minutes total, rather than accepting ELIXIR-DEV's two incomplete attempts): `mix test` -- Finished in 1656.9 seconds. Result: 3204/3208 passed (6/6 properties, 3198/3202 tests), 21 excluded, 4 failed. All 4 failures structurally attributed, none are regressions from this diff:
   a. `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest` (1 test): 'found 3 new violation(s)' -- traced to `[H3] non-schema top-level key(s): ["next_action"]` on THREE PRE-EXISTING handoff files in this same run (`step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json`, `step-02-code-designer.json`, `step-02b-code-design-validator.json`), committed at `cb8299c2` early in this workflow run, before any of the poller/admission code changes existed and absent from `main`. This is a handoff-bookkeeping schema issue in this run's own earlier artifacts, not a code regression from the ISS-0421 fix -- outside this gate's idiom/OTP mandate, flagging for whichever agent owns run hygiene rather than blocking on it here.
   b. `Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreakerTest` (1 test): `Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` failed (got a live pid) after the breaker had already reached `:open` (the preceding `wait_for_breaker_open()` assertion passed). Investigated directly: the `:force_poller_crash` raise this test relies on fires at poller.ex line 218-220, inside `handle_info(:tick, state)`, BEFORE `fetch_tenant_schemas/0` or any `run_sweep/4` call -- i.e. before any code this diff touches ever executes for that tick. Re-ran this test file in isolation 3 times (`mix test test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs --seed 0`): 1 passed, 3/3, no flake. This is consistent with a timing-sensitive flake under the full suite's heavy resource contention (3208 tests, many spinning up/tearing down tenant Postgres schemas concurrently) rather than a structural regression -- the crash trigger and the property under test are both upstream of this diff's changes.
   c/d. `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` rust-pin tests (2 tests): `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- rustc is not on PATH in this sandbox, exactly the documented pre-existing rustc-toolchain-gap this project's README already calls out as a known sandbox limitation, unrelated to any application code.

6. IDIOM / SUPERVISION / SCOPE VERDICT ON THE FULL DIFF (original approved parts + this rework, re-confirmed): unchanged from step-04's assessment of the rest of the diff, now re-verified against the corrected, final code.
   - Supervision: unaffected. No new process outside the existing `Poller` GenServer; `Task.async_stream/3`'s task pool at all 7 sweep call sites is bounded, fully consumed, and time-bounded (`on_timeout: :kill_task`). No orphaned/unsupervised long-lived process. `Letflow.InstanceSupervisor`-per-instance isolation is untouched -- this change is scheduler/admission internals only.
   - Idiomatic vs. crutch: `global_cap/1` and `reserved_headroom/1` are both trivial, idiomatic `GenServer.call` accessors over existing state, added because a real caller (Poller) needs the live value -- not premature abstraction. `run_sweep/4` centralizes 6 identically-shaped call sites; still good factoring, not new framework machinery.
   - Scope creep: none introduced by this rework. It extends a pattern the design already established once (`reserved_headroom/1`) to the one place it was missing, per my own step-04 routing -- no new behaviours, macros, or generic plumbing appeared.
   - Type-safety: no new class of invalid state. Not filing a new issue.
   - GenServer.call-per-task-dispatch question (explicitly re-examined this pass): NOT a new overhead or failure-mode concern. `Admission.global_cap()`/`Admission.reserved_headroom()` are each evaluated exactly ONCE per sweep per tick -- as a plain Elixir function-call argument to `run_sweep/4`, evaluated before `Task.async_stream/3` starts, not once per schema/task. That is 7 additional `GenServer.call`s to `Admission` per tick total (6 gated sweeps + 1 unwrapped sweep), negligible next to the O(schemas) `try_acquire`/`release` calls `with_admission/3` already issues to the same `Admission` process per schema per operation, which this diff's design already accounts for. If `Admission` were slow or unavailable, these 7 calls would block synchronously inside `Poller`'s own `handle_info/2` just as the pre-existing per-schema acquire/release calls already do -- this is not a qualitatively new dependency or failure mode, since a tick already fully depends on `Admission` being responsive via those existing calls.

VERDICT: PASS. The design gap I found at step-04 is genuinely closed in the real, final code -- not merely claimed closed. No changes to `test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` were made at any point in this rework, satisfying my original constraint.

ROUTING: to TEST-DESIGNER. Two coverage items carried forward from step-04 (not new, restating so they aren't lost at the handoff boundary):
   - Add regression coverage for `Letflow.Admission.global_cap/1` tracking a NON-default configured value (mirroring the equivalent gap already flagged for `reserved_headroom/1`) -- close both live-derivation call sites' coverage gap in the same pass, per step-04's original routing note.
   - The hardcoded-literal-regression mutation I and ELIXIR-DEV both independently re-verified by hand this pass (sed-substituting the literal `8` back in and confirming the same 4 REQ-218 tests fail) is not yet a permanent automated test -- worth a lightweight regression test that asserts the gated sweeps' `max_concurrency` argument is NOT a hardcoded constant equal to today's default `global_cap`, so a future literal-reintroduction is caught by CI without requiring another manual mutation pass.
   - Not mine to route further, but noting for completeness: the `[H3] next_action` handoff-lint violations on this run's own step-01/02/02b files (item 6a above) are a pre-existing, non-code issue in this run's artifacts and are outside REVIEWER's OTP/idiom mandate.

Independently confirmed the live-derivation fix in the real diff, independently re-ran the 31 previously-affected tests (31/31), independently re-ran the mutation test (same 4 REQ-218 tests fail with the literal reintroduced, confirmed via my own sed edit and revert), and ran the full suite to completion myself (3204/3208 passed, 21 excluded, 4 failed -- 1 pre-existing handoff-lint issue from this run's own earlier artifacts, 1 flaky-under-load PollersBreaker timing test unrelated to this diff's changed code paths (isolated re-run 3/3 passed), 2 pre-existing rustc-toolchain-gap sandbox failures). No new supervision, idiom, or scope-creep concerns; GenServer.call-per-sweep overhead assessed as negligible and not a new failure mode. PASS -- routed to TEST-DESIGNER.
